af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.0: §7Prints §fchip wafers§7 through a §freticle§7 (not consumed), one mode per substrate:
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.2: §780-65nm: the §fMk2 Photolithography Scanner§7. 50nm and finer: the §fOrbital Lithography Station§7.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.3: §7A substrate prints its own chips and all lower ones as GT's wafers, §fmore per print§7 the higher it is.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.4: §7Takes §fcoated wafers§7 (§fCoater Track§7: prime, BARC, resist, topcoat, bake): §dexpose §8> §bbake §8> §bdevelop §8> §betch §8> §brinse
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.5: §bVacuum§7: starts at §f0§7 when formed and pumps to §f100§7 in §f10s per version§7 (V1 10s ... V3 30s).
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.6: §7Prints only start on a §fsealed§7 vacuum; without power it vents to 0 in §c60s§7. Every print can §cbreak§7:
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.7: §7the finer the node, the likelier (§f2%%§7 at 350nm ... §f5%%§7 at 100nm), §c+50%%§7 if the vacuum vents mid-print.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.8: §6Versions 1-3§7, like the Assembly Line: one more lens slice each (§f3-5§7), §f10-12§7 blocks long;
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.9: §7the light source allows up to: §fpurple lamp§7 V1, §fKrF laser§7 V2, §fArF laser§7 V3.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.10: §7Per version above a mode: §a0.8x time§7, §a0.75x break chance§7.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.11: §7Light: mercury i-line (350nm), KrF excimer (200nm), ArF excimer (100nm).
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.12: §7Power: up to §f2 Energy Hatches§7; a print needs 4A of the mode's tier (two normal hatches). §aPerfect OC§7, §fbatch mode§7.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.13: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f8§7 fluid input, §f1§7 maintenance, §f2+2§7 item buses at the controller.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.14: §7Built from §fPlascrete§7 with §fPlascrete Pipe§7 and §fFilter Casings§7; it needs no Cleanroom.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.15: §cWafers contaminate in a player's inventory§7: wear §fRubber Gloves§7 or work in a Cleanroom.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.0: §7Step-and-scan exposure of the §f80nm§7 and §f65nm§7 nodes through a §freticle§7 (not consumed):
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.1: §e80nm§7 Trinium (ArF, NA 0.93), §e65nm§7 Naquadria (ArF in water immersion, NA 1.2).
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.2: §6Versions 1-2§7: a cleanroom tube §f10-12§7 blocks long with §f2-3§7 window sections (4 Cleanroom Glass each).
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.3: §7Per version above a mode: §a0.8x time§7, §a0.75x break chance§7.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.4: §bVacuum§7 like the line's: prints wait for the seal (§f40s§7 V1, §f50s§7 V2 from 0); it vents in §c60s§7 without power.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.5: §7Breaks §f7%%§7 (80nm) and §f9%%§7 (65nm), up to §c+50%%§7 if the vacuum vents mid-print.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.6: §7Power: up to §f2 Energy Hatches§7; a print needs 4A of the mode's tier. §aPerfect OC§7, §fbatch mode§7.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.7: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum, on any plascrete: §f2§7 energy, §f8§7 fluid input, §f1§7 maintenance, §f2+2§7 item buses.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.8: §7Its §dArF Excimer Laser§7 goes in a slot of its screen (not used up). Gearbox wafer stages, pipe-casing track lines under §fPlascrete Filter Casings§7; no Cleanroom needed.
§7Prints the finest nodes: §e50nm§7 Neutronium, §e20nm§7 Transmuted Nt, §e7nm§7 Strange Matter, §f1nm§7 Chromodynium (§dMk2 only§7).
§cOnly works in orbit§7 (e.g. Ad Astra's Earth Orbit). The controller §ffaces up§7 out of the top deck (look down to place it); the station turns with it.
§7Power: §f1 Laser Hatch§7 and up to §f3 Energy Hatches§7: 4A of the node's tier, §e50A of UHV§7 at 1nm.
§bCoolant§7 through §fCoolant Hatches§7, every print: §bSupercooled§7 Hydrogen < Argon < Xenon < §dEndion§7 (Cryostat; not the dense fluids).
§7Best: 50nm §fSupercooled Xenon§7, the rest §fSupercooled Endion§7. Each grade colder than the minimum: §a0.8x break chance§7, §a0.9x time§7.
§d7nm§7 and §f1nm§7 draw §fcomputation§7 (32 / 96 CWU/t, §fComputation Hatch§7). Every §f1nm§7 print needs its own §fresearch§7 (a data orb in a §fData Hatch§7).
§7The §freticle§7 goes in the station's reticle slot (kept; not from buses). 20nm and 7nm need an §fEUV Light Source§7 in its EUV slot, 1nm a §fDry Resist Cartridge§7 per wafer.
§bNo vacuum to pump§7, it is space: switched on and powered, it §fstarts up in 10s§7. Breaks §f12%%§7 (50nm) to §f35%%§7 (1nm).
§bMagnetic field§7: switched on and powered, the station itself (and 4 blocks above the deck) has §fnormal gravity§7.
§7Parts only on the §fPTFE top deck§7, optional with a maximum: §f1§7 laser, §f3§7 energy, §f8§7 fluid, §f2§7 coolant, §f1§7 computation, §f1§7 data, buses, §f1§7 maintenance.
§7A §f25x25§7 platform, §f18§7 deep: GCYM casings, HSS-S trusses and an HSS-G undulator mast. A light ring glows while it prints: §cdo not touch it§7.
§aPerfect overclocks§7, §fbatch mode§7: prints overclocked below 5s run several at once. Every wafer rolls its own break.

§dArray Mk2§7: a §fscrewdriver§7 on the controller switches to the §f35x35§7 extended platform (the same station with its rim, trusses and beams moved out, and a larger light ring). Only the Mk2 runs §dplasma atomic soldering§7.
§dPlasma soldering§7 is no longer done here: the §fHyper-Intensity Laser Engraver§7 runs it.
§dMk2 only§7: the §f1 nm§7 prints (chromodynium). The basic station cannot start them, and its mode tab keeps them shut.

§dBeam focus§7 (Mk2): it §faligns§7 after start-up (the Mk2's own work waits for §f25%§7), a running recipe §fdrifts§7 it and every run costs a little. §fComputation to spare§7 on the hatches holds it; §fsharp§7 (60%) and §flocked§7 (90%) focus shorten runs and cut the break chance.

§dFocus lock§7 (option, §fsneak + screwdriver§7 on the controller): once the focus is full it §flatches§7 and stays until the station is broken, no drift, no cost per run. It needs a §fsupplemental power connection§7: an energy hatch (§fEV+§7, not the laser hatch) with 2,048 EU/t spare. Without it for 5 s the lock lets go.
af9.advanced_circuit_manufacturer.toolti: §7The circuit plant of the Genesis pack. It makes the §dPico circuits§7: board, cleansed board, CPU, organized circuit, casing and rack.
§7Recipes of up to §f16§7 items and §f4§7 fluids; §fcomputation§7 through a §fComputation Hatch§7. §aPerfect OC§7; a §fParallel Hatch§7 multiplies the runs.
§7The Pico recipes draw §e300A of UHV§7: a §fLaser Hatch§7 carries that.
§7Parts on any §fLarge-Scale Assembler Casing§7, optional with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f1§7 laser, §f4+2§7 item buses, §f4§7 fluid, §f1§7 computation, §f1§7 parallel, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.dtpf.tooltip.0: §7An industrial skeleton §f37x29x37§7 that forges plasma into matter: four lattice pylons, a plasma core braced by crossing diagonal struts, rings of beams, box girders and a diagonal cross on top.
af9.dtpf.tooltip.1: §6Running-time ramp§7: the longer it runs without a pause, the cheaper and faster it forges: up to §f-50%% EU/t§7 and §f-25%% time§7 after §f30 minutes§7. A pause cools it three times as fast as it warmed.
af9.dtpf.tooltip.2: §7Runs only a recipe its hatches can §ffully supply§7. Perfect overclocks. §fUHV§7 recipes.
af9.dtpf.tooltip.3: §7Every block of the low §fwall§7 (fusion casing, round the edge) may be a hatch: up to §f4§7 energy, §f8§7 fluid input, §f4§7 fluid output, §f4§7 item buses each way, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.dtpf.tooltip.4: §7The ionised matter is §dstrange matter plasma§7 and §dchromodynium plasma§7, made here from their dust and §dEndion§7.
af9.dtpf.tooltip.5: §7After GTNH's Dimensionally Transcendent Plasma Forge, built differently.
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.0: §7A power plant after GTNH Intergalactic's §fDyson Swarm§7 (the same §f16x20x16§7 structure): put §fsails§7 in an input bus and they fly on in the swarm. The receiver turns what they catch into power for the §foutput hatches§7.
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.1: §6Sails§7, lowest to highest: §eAllthemodium§7 §f100%%§7, §5Unobtainium Alloy§7 §f200%%§7, §dChromodynium Star Matter Tritan Alloy§7 §f350%%§7 of the base yield, §f262,144 EU/t§7 a sail. Up to §f10,000§7 sails.
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.2: §7The light of the dimension scales it (§fOverworld 100%%§7, §fVenus 176%%§7, §fMars 81%%§7, the Nether none). A cycle takes §f360 B§7 of §bsupercooled hydrogen§7 for §f1 hour§7.
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.3: §7At the end of a cycle collisions destroy some sails: more sails collide more, a §fcomputation hatch§7 steers them clear (GTNH's formula).
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.4: §7Hatch spots: §fpower output§7 (energy or laser source) in the receiver base, §fsail bus and coolant hatch§7 in the deployment unit base, §fcomputation§7 in the command centre base.
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.5: §7Feeds the §fUHV+ lines§7: UHV recipes take §f100 A§7 of UHV power, XPS §f300 A§7, NVM §f1,000 A§7.
af9.dyson_swarm.tooltip.6: §7A §fplunger§7 on the controller takes sails back (lowest tier first, as many as it has uses left; sneak to drop what does not fit).
af9.space_mining_module_mk1.tooltip.0: §7GTNH's elevator module as a small multiblock of its own: put it in a §fmodule slot§7 of a Space Elevator (the casings above and below it are the slot's, hatches go there).
af9.space_mining_module_mk1.tooltip.1: §7The tower finds it when it forms and §fconnects§7 it; its screen says whether the motors power it. A powered module flies §f2§7 expeditions at once in the elevator's runs.
af9.space_mining_module_mk1.tooltip.2: §7Needs motors of its own tier or better; the motors power as many modules as they have slots (best tier first).
af9.space_mining_module_mk2.tooltip.0: §7GTNH's elevator module as a small multiblock of its own: put it in a §fmodule slot§7 of a Space Elevator (the casings above and below it are the slot's, hatches go there).
af9.space_mining_module_mk2.tooltip.1: §7The tower finds it when it forms and §fconnects§7 it; its screen says whether the motors power it. A powered module flies §f4§7 expeditions at once in the elevator's runs.
af9.space_mining_module_mk2.tooltip.2: §7Needs motors of its own tier or better; the motors power as many modules as they have slots (best tier first).
af9.space_mining_module_mk3.tooltip.0: §7GTNH's elevator module as a small multiblock of its own: put it in a §fmodule slot§7 of a Space Elevator (the casings above and below it are the slot's, hatches go there).
af9.space_mining_module_mk3.tooltip.1: §7The tower finds it when it forms and §fconnects§7 it; its screen says whether the motors power it. A powered module flies §f8§7 expeditions at once in the elevator's runs.
af9.space_mining_module_mk3.tooltip.2: §7Needs motors of its own tier or better; the motors power as many modules as they have slots (best tier first).
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.0: §7A §fRotary Hearth Furnace§7 rebuilt as a standalone multi: the same §f13x17x13§7 hearth, running only §cSanguinite§7.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.1: §cNeither the EBF nor the Rotary Hearth can smelt sanguinite§7: the hot-ingot print lives on §fgtceu:sanguinite_hearth§7 only.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.2: §6A heat mass, not an instant furnace§7: it preheats toward its coils' maximum (§fcoil temp + 100K per hatch tier above MV§7) in §f60s§7 while on and powered.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.3: §7Prints only start §fpreheated§7 (§f13000 K§7): a cold hearth waits once, then an enabled, powered hearth §aholds its heat§7 and smelts back-to-back.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.4: §7Resonant Endion coils (§f12600 K§7) with UV hatches reach §f13100 K§7: just past the smelt. Breaking the structure §cvents it cold§7.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.5: §7Smelt: §f14 crude + circuit 10 + 50000 supercooled endion§7 (the quench) -> §c14 hot ingots§7, §f4A UV§7, §f60s§7. The Bulk Blast Chiller finishes them.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.6: §7Automate it: keep it §fon under power§7 (ME level emitter on the crude stock, or a clock) and it stays hot and self-starts.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.7: §7Up to §f1 parallel hatch§7 multiplies the 14-ingot prints. §aPerfect OC§7, §fbatch mode§7. Heaters draw §f1/8 A§7 on top.
af9.sanguinite_hearth_furnace.tooltip.8: §7Parts on any §fhigh-temperature smelting casing§7, maximums only: up to §f4§7 energy, §f2+2§7 buses, §f4§7 fluid, §f1§7 parallel, §f1§7 maintenance, §f1§7 muffler.
af9.orbital_array.mk2.on: Array Mk2 (extended) switched on: rebuild as 35x35
af9.orbital_array.mk2.off: Basic station switched on: rebuild as 25x25
af9.orbital_array.mk2.busy: Stop the run before switching sizes
af9.orbital_array.mode_mk2_only: Orbital Array Mk2 only: switch the station to its extended size first (a screwdriver on the controller)
af9.orbital_array.lock.on: Focus lock on: once the beams are fully focused they latch until the station is broken. It needs a supplemental power connection: an EV or better energy hatch (not the laser hatch) with %s EU/t spare.
af9.orbital_array.lock.off: Focus lock off: the focus drifts and has to be held by computation
af9.hile.tooltip.0: §7GTNH's §fIndustrial Laser Engraver§7 as a §f5x5x5§7 plasma soldering station: the laser comes from the §flaser target hatch§7 at the top, down the glass shaft, onto the §fLaser Resistant Plate§7.
af9.hile.tooltip.1: §7Runs §dplasma soldering§7: UHV+ circuits deposited ion-by-ion with §dPlasma Solder§7, no reflow. The UHV mainframe takes §f100 A§7 of UHV, so the laser hatch must carry it.
af9.hile.tooltip.2: §7Perfect overclocks; a parallel hatch multiplies the runs. Any glass tier works.
af9.hile.tooltip.3: §7Any §fLaser Containment Casing§7 may be an energy hatch, item bus, fluid hatch, parallel hatch or maintenance hatch.
af9.hile.tooltip.4: §7After GTNH's Industrial Laser Engraver, built block for block.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.1: §bDense Cooling§7: gas to dense liquid (4:1), the intermediate.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.2: §dSupercooling§7: the dense liquid to a supercooled fluid, rated at §b-5000 K§7.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.3: §7Hydrogen, argon, xenon and §5endion§7 (from the End's air).
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.4: §cNeeds 4A of HV§7 (two normal Energy Hatches) to run at all. §aPerfect OC§7.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.6: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f2+2§7 fluid hatches, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.staged_assembly.tooltip.0: §7Builds its recipes in stages: every stage is fed separately.
af9.staged_assembly.tooltip.1: §7A stage only runs with §fexactly its inputs§7 in the hatches; the console names the waiting stage.
af9.staged_assembly.tooltip.2: §fEMI§7 shows every stage with its inputs. §aPerfect OC§7.
af9.staged_assembly.tooltip.3: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f2+2§7 item buses, §f2§7 fluid hatches, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.0: §7A storage ring §f47§7 blocks across and §f7§7 high: an §fempty beam tube§7 in a clean-steel shell (the bending magnets), four glass gates.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.1: §aNeutron Irradiation§7: a spallation neutron beam turns §fNeutronium-doped Wafers§7
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.3: §6Heavy-Ion Collision§7: lead ions collide, the §fquark-gluon plasma§7 goes into magnetic traps.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.4: §dQuark Synthesis§7: quark-gluon plasma condenses into §fStrange Matter§7, then §fChromodynium§7.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.5: §7Fluids: §fCoolant Hatches only§7 (supercooled hydrogen, argon, xenon, endion). A recipe takes its coolant §for any colder one§7.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.6: §7Power: up to §f4§7 Energy Hatches or §f2§7 Laser Hatches, with the recipe's full EU/t.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.7: §7Parts go §fanywhere on the clean-steel casing§7, optional with a maximum: §f2§7 coolant hatches, §f2+2§7 item buses, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.8: §7While it runs, its beam glows in the tube (see it through the gates' glass). Beam energy grows with the voltage tier.
af9.coolant_hatch.tooltip.1: §7The only fluid input of the Particle Accelerator, the Orbital Lithography Station and the Space Elevator's coolant input.
af9.wireless_receiver.tooltip.0: §7Energy input hatch for any multiblock, fed by a linked §bWireless Energy Transmitter§7: any distance, any dimension.
af9.wireless_receiver.tooltip.1: §7No voltage of its own: works at the transmitter's voltage and draws up to §f%sA§7.
af9.wireless_receiver.tooltip.2: §7Link: right-click the transmitter with a §fData Stick§7, then this hatch (shift-right-click copies its link).
af9.wireless_transmitter.tooltip.0: §7Output hatch for the §fPower Substation§7 (or any multiblock that puts out energy): feeds every linked §bWireless Energy Receiver§7.
af9.wireless_transmitter.tooltip.1: §7Sends at the highest voltage of the multiblock's energy inputs, up to §f%sA§7 (no inputs: set the voltage on its screen).
af9.wireless_transmitter.tooltip.2: §7Right-click it with a §fData Stick§7 to take the link to the receivers.
gtceu.staged_assembly.desc: Recipes built in stages, every stage fed separately
gtceu.ion_collision.desc: Lead ions collide into quark-gluon plasma
gtceu.quark_synthesis.desc: Quark-gluon plasma condenses into strange matter and chromodynium
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.0: §7The semiconductor-grade reactor: fab chemistry runs §fonly§7 in SMC machines.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.2: §aFilter ceiling (Plascrete or GT Filter Casings): its own clean room (ISO 5). Sterile filters: ISO 3 and 2 parallels.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.3: §6One heating coil in the jacket: each coil tier above Cupronickel saves 1/20 of the EU/t (at most half).
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.4: §dProduct changeover: the first run of a different recipe also takes 1000mB Nitrogen or Argon, 5s more.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.5: §7Perfect overclocks, batch mode. Takes one Parallel Hatch and one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.6: §7The vessel is open (only the stirrer and the coil): while it runs it shows §9Water§7 (wet processing), §bDistilled Water§7 (blending) or §cDestabilized Redstone§7 (synthesis).
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.0: §7Packed column for fab gases and solvents, with a cold box for cryogenic work.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.2: §aEvery tray layer (PTFE Pipe Casing) is a parallel: 1-8 trays.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.3: §aFilter hood (Plascrete or GT Filter Casings): its own clean room (ISO 5, sterile filters ISO 3).
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.4: §dProduct changeover: 2000mB Nitrogen and 5s more on the first run of a different recipe.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.5: §7Cuts go to any fluid output hatch. Batch mode, one Parallel Hatch, one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.0: §7Filter-press stack of membrane cells between titanium electrodes.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.2: §aEvery cell (PTFE Pipe Casing between two Titanium Frames) is a parallel: 1-8 cells.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.3: §aFilter ceiling (Plascrete or GT Filter Casings): its own clean room (ISO 5, sterile filters ISO 3).
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.4: §dProduct changeover: the cells are flushed with 1000mB Distilled Water, 5s more.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.5: §7Batch mode, one Parallel Hatch, one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_thermal_processing_furnace.toolt: §7A horizontal tube furnace: calciners, CVD reactors and Czochralski pullers under inert gas.
§6Heats like the Electric Blast Furnace: coil temperature, +100K per energy tier above MV, EBF overclocks.
§dProduct changeover: 1000mB Argon or Nitrogen and 10s more on the first run of a different recipe.
§7No clean room needed. Batch mode, one Parallel Hatch, one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_chemical_reactor.tooltip.0: §7Fab chemistry: §fSynthesis§7, §fBlending§7, §fWet Processing§7. GT's reactors cannot make it.
af9.smc_chemical_reactor.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the first run of a different recipe takes 1000mB Nitrogen or Argon, 5s more.
af9.smc_chemical_reactor.tooltip.2: §eFrom HV power on, the recipes need a Cleanroom.
af9.smc_fractionating_still.tooltip.0: §7Batch still: §fFractionation§7 (one column cut per run, circuit = cut) and §fPurification§7.
af9.smc_fractionating_still.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the first run of a different recipe takes 2000mB Nitrogen, 5s more.
af9.smc_fractionating_still.tooltip.2: §eFrom HV power on, the recipes need a Cleanroom.
af9.smc_electrolytic_cell.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the cell is flushed with 1000mB Distilled Water, 5s more.
af9.smc_electrolytic_cell.tooltip.2: §eFrom HV power on, the recipes need a Cleanroom.
af9.smc_thermal_furnace.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the first run of a different recipe takes 1000mB Argon or Nitrogen, 10s more.
af9.smc_thermal_furnace.tooltip.temperat: §6Reaches §f%sK§6, the heat of its tier's coil.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.0: §7GTNH's tower on a cable into space: it sends §bMining Drones§7 to the asteroids and brings the ore home. The pack's renewable ore source.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.1: §7A §bMining Drone§7 (not used up) in the drone slot of its screen, §e50-100 buckets§7 of §bhydrogen§7 and of a §bsupercooled coolant§7 (hydrogen, argon, xenon, endion by tier; into §fCoolant Hatches§7) and §e4-32 amps of ZPM§7 for minutes.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.2: §7Out comes a random asteroid: §etens of stacks§7 of raw ore, made from GT's ore veins (the best drone also finds the exotic asteroid, of the ores no vein holds).
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.3: §7Mk1 reaches the Overworld's ores, Mk2 the Nether's, Mk3 the End's, Mk4 the Asteroid Field's and the exotic ones. A better drone also gets more stacks.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.4: §7Mk1 runs on one ZPM hatch (4A), Mk2 on two, Mk3 on four hatches (16A), Mk4 needs a laser hatch (32A).
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.5: §735x35x43, GTNH's structure block for block: a floor of §fUltra High Strength Concrete§7, a tapering frame of §fBase Casing§7 and §fStress-Proof Casing§7 round a column of §bMotors§7 (88, all of one tier) with the §fCable§7 on top of its shaft, under the open sky. Formed, the cable runs up into the sky and the §bclimber§7 rides it.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.6: §7Hatches (maxima, any tier; ZPM ones fit the expeditions): 4 energy and 2 laser in the bottom centre casings; 4 §fCoolant Hatches§7, 8 fluid input, 6 fluid output, 2 item input and 12 item output there or in the module slots.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.7: §bSpace Mining Modules§7 in the 12 module slots fly the expeditions, as in GTNH: MK-I 2 at once, MK-II 4, MK-III 8, each with the full hydrogen, coolant and energy. The §bMotors§7' tier powers 6 / 12 / 15 / 18 / 24 slots and modules up to its own tier. Without a powered module nothing flies.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.8: §7Two sizes, as in GTNH (the size switch is on the controller's screen): the basic tower, or §eextended§7 with a ring of 47x47 round its foot and §b12 more module slots§7 (24). Motors MK-III and better have the slots for them.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.9: §7Or a §bliquid mission§7 (the arrows on its screen pick it): the same flight to a planet for one fluid of GTNH's Space Pumping table, §e8 to 17,920 buckets§7 a mission, into §ffluid output hatches§7. Mk1 reaches planet types 2-3, Mk2 4-5 (the oils, helium-3), Mk3 6-7 (deuterium, tritium), Mk4 type 8.
af9.space_elevator.tooltip.10: §8After GTNH's Space Elevator (GTNH Intergalactic: minecraft7771, BlueWeabo; its design: Sampsa, Jimbno, Adam, Baunti). The screen says what it lacks while nothing flies.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.16: §dMulti-patterning§7: a §fscrewdriver§7 on the controller lets it print the mode one version above its own, exposing every layer twice: §c2x time§7, §c1.5x breaks§7, 2x OPC.
af9.photolithography_scanner.tooltip.9: §dMulti-patterning§7: a §fscrewdriver§7 on the controller lets a V1 scanner print 65nm, exposing every layer twice: §c2x time§7, §c1.5x breaks§7, 2x OPC. Takes §fcoated wafers§7 (Coater Track).
af9.fx1_reactor.tooltip.0: §7A fission reactor: a §fFuel Rod§7, §fDistilled Water§7 and §fSodium-Potassium§7 coolant in; §bSupercritical Steam§7, the §cSpent Fuel Rod§7 and hot coolant out.
af9.fx1_reactor.tooltip.1: §7One rod per 1,200 ticks makes §f61,440 mB§7 of steam: Large Steam Turbines (and Extreme Reactors' turbines) turn it into power.
af9.fx1_reactor.tooltip.2: §7The hot alloy goes back to coolant in a §fVacuum Freezer§7. The spent rod holds the §dplutonium§7: macerate, dissolve in nitric acid, centrifuge.
af9.fx1_reactor.tooltip.3: §cRadioactive§7: while it runs, a warning shows above the hotbar near it. Wear a full hazmat suit.
af9.fx1_reactor.tooltip.5: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f1+1§7 item, §f3§7 + §f4§7 fluid hatches, §f1§7 maintenance.
